name: K3 Flight
tagline: Run the Kimi K3 2.8T model locally on CPU with ~55GB RAM
description: K3 Flight is a single-file Linux inference server that runs Kimi K3 — a 2.8-trillion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model — locally on CPU with a measured runtime memory of about 55GB, powered by cPilot Runtime. The complete 929GB checkpoint stays on storage; the runtime stages weights and execution state into a much smaller live working set because each token only activates 16 of 896 experts. It is not compression and not a smaller model — the full Q2_K checkpoint executes without keeping 929GB resident. The preview targets Linux x86-64 with 64GB+ RAM and a fast NVMe SSD, exposes an OpenAI-compatible API plus a web UI, and deliberately does not claim datacenter latency: prefill is roughly 1 token/s and decode around 0.8 token/s on the reference run. The project publishes honest numbers and invites reproducible community runs.
highlights: Runs the complete 2.8T-parameter Kimi K3 Q2_K checkpoint on CPU with ~55GB measured runtime RAM
cPilot Runtime stages weights from storage — no need for 929GB resident, no compression trick
Single-file Linux inference server with OpenAI-compatible API and web UI
Targets 64GB+ RAM and NVMe storage on Linux x86-64, no GPU required
Honest benchmark posture: ~1 token/s prefill, ~0.8 token/s decode, invites community hardware reports
curatorNote: The most audacious local-LLM claim of the week — running a 2.8T model in 55GB of RAM is a systems problem, not a memory problem, and cPilot treats it that way. 899 stars in days, with refreshingly honest throughput numbers.
